mode1_vs_mode2_note: The batch/motor run (Mode 1, results/agent_batch/OWL-NEXUS5-CASE_agent_bundle.json) reports verdict=NOISE. Root cause (diagnosed in this session, not fixed here): vigia/pipeline/vigia_integration_bridge.py::_normalize_artifact_legacy() and vigia/tools/vigia_case_adapter.py::artifact_to_signal() expect a legacy artifact schema (artifact_id, forensic_anomalies:list, analyst_flags:list, peirce_layer) that does not match this case's schema (id, content:dict, metadata.significance). Every .get(key, default) silently falls through, so all 20 signals in the Mode-1 bundle carry artifact_id='?', evidence_type='unknown', confidence=1/2, z_score=0/1 -- an ingestion/adapter defect, not a miscalibrated threshold. This Mode 2 bundle resolves the case independently by reading the actual device data directly; per CLAUDE.md, both outputs are preserved, neither silently overrides the other.
known_limitations: mount_sift_evidence (MCP tool) is unusable in this deployment: vigia/vigia_sift_bridge.py:1251-1262 requires mount_point to simultaneously resolve under VIGIA_EVIDENCE_DIR (path sanitizer) AND under the hardcoded /mnt/analysis (_MOUNT_ROOT check) -- mutually exclusive constraints, no path satisfies both. It also requires the MCP server process to run as root (os.geteuid()==0), which it does not. The operator performed the raw-image mount and app-directory extraction manually via sudo, outside the MCP, strictly read-only (ro,noload,noexec,nosuid,nodev) and with a hard link (same inode) to the original acquisition file, preserving chain of custody; all subsequent analysis (list_files/search_pattern/generate_forensic_hash) was done via MCP.

methodological_disclaimer: IMPORTANT, added after external adversarial audit (relayed by operator via a separate ChatGPT review, 2026-07-21): the tool_execution_log below (both the original 29 entries and the 8 correction entries appended here) was constructed by the Claude Code agent AFTER each batch of real MCP tool calls completed within this conversation, by writing a short Python script that calls ToolExecutionLogChain.append() once per remembered call, back-to-back in one process. This means: (a) entry_hash/entry_hmac chaining IS real -- it proves no entry was altered relative to its neighbours once written, and the SHA-256/HMAC of each cited artifact IS real and independently reproducible; but (b) the per-entry 'timestamp' field does NOT represent the wall-clock moment each MCP tool was actually invoked during the conversation -- entries within a batch are seconds-to-microseconds apart because they were authored in one script run, not captured live at each call site. The bundle's analysis_timestamp field can therefore precede its own tool_execution_log batch, which is confusing and was flagged correctly by the external audit. This is a real gap between 'tamper-evident once written' and 'contemporaneously captured' -- the fix is to instrument vigia_sift_bridge.py itself to call chain.append() at each tool's entry/exit (not done in this session; recommended as follow-up, out of scope for resolving this case).

v1_corrections.correction: RECLASSIFIED to UNRESOLVED. Pidgin (the exact IM client named in the corrected SMS above) is installed and was run on this machine (3 prefetch entries: PIDGIN.EXE-86E18E41.pf, PIDGIN-2.11.0.EXE-93DF4765.pf, 'PIDGIN-2.11.0 (1).EXE-138939A7.pf'). Precise execution timestamps could not be extracted (prefetch files are MAM-compressed, Windows 10 format; no decompressor available in this toolset). search_pattern for 'mcavoy'/'Sarah'/'layster' across the full owl-2019-hd1-windows tree found zero ASCII hits, but this is INCONCLUSIVE, not a refutation: Windows registry hives (SAM/SOFTWARE/SYSTEM/NTUSER.DAT) commonly store strings as UTF-16LE, which a plain ASCII grep will not match even if present.
v1_corrections.impact: The Daubert Corroboration Gate's premise ('no second independent device/channel in evidence') is therefore UNCONFIRMED rather than affirmatively established. The verdict is NOT upgraded on this basis -- the gap is disclosed as open, not resolved in either direction. Resolving it needs either a prefetch decompressor + timeline correlation, or a UTF-16-aware string search of the Windows registry hives, neither performed in this session.

v1_corrections.issue: v1 report language ('HMAC-sealed, independently verified with verify_tool_log.py') implied the audit trail proves real-time capture of 29 actual MCP calls.
v1_corrections.correction: See methodological_disclaimer above. verify_tool_log.py verifies chain/HMAC integrity of the entries as written; it does not and cannot verify that the entries were captured live, in real time, at each tool call. Re-running verify_tool_log.py WITHOUT --hmac-key-file (as the external audit did) also cannot confirm the HMAC layer -- that requires the key file, which is deliberately access-restricted (that is by design, not a flaw, but must be stated, not assumed).
